refuters.argument:
After a clause-by-clause comparison I found no place where the Lean statement SM.star_generic_law (work/reviews/lem-star-generic-reviewer-input-statement.lean.txt, lines 22-41) is weaker than, adds a hypothesis to, or quantifies differently from lem:star-generic (reference/SM/sm-5-transport.tex 16-33); every local definition denotes the printed object.

The two focus points:

(1) Tangency clause, source (ii): "Every edge line of K_r is tangent to the circle of radius rho = cos(pi r/N) about the origin, at the midpoint of the edge". Lean (lines 29-32): for every i, euclideanLength (edgePoint (star r) i (1/2)) = starRadius r, planeDot (edgePoint (star r) i (1/2)) (edge (star r) i) = 0, and for all t : R, starRadius r <= euclideanLength (edgePoint (star r) i t) with equality iff t = 1/2. Expanding: edgePoint P i t = P i + t • edge P i (Polygon.lean:51-52), edge P i = P (i+1) - P i (Polygon.lean:49), so {edgePoint t : t in R} is exactly the edge line and edgePoint (1/2) is the midpoint (mu_i + mu_{i+1})/2; euclideanLength = the Euclidean norm via C (EuclideanPlane.lean:29-34), planeDot = the dot product (EuclideanPlane.lean:27), starRadius r = cos(pi r/(2r+1)) (StarPolygons.lean:41). A line is tangent to the circle |x| = rho at m iff m is on the circle and the line is perpendicular to the radius Om (equivalently, iff m is the unique point of the line on the closed disc). The Lean asserts both formulations simultaneously: |m| = rho, m . edge = 0, and the unique-nearest-point clause. The unique-nearest clause also forces edge != 0 (a constant line would make the iff false), so the "edge line" is a genuine line. Hence the Lean clause is equivalent to (in fact at least as strong as) the printed tangency; nothing is weaker. The trailing strictlyLeft (star r) i 0 := 0 < det (edge P i) (0 - P i) (Chirotope.lean:24-25) is exactly the lem:chi-basic(iii) naming convention ("strictly to the left of the directed line through E_i if sgn det(l_i, mu_k - mu_i) = +1", sm-1-polygons.tex:80-83) applied to the origin, matching "the origin lies strictly to the left of every directed edge".

(2) Bow-tie tuple order, source (iv): "(chi_123, chi_124, chi_134, chi_234) = (+1,-1,-1,+1)". Lean line 37-38: (chi bowTie 1 2 3, chi bowTie 1 2 4, chi bowTie 1 3 4, chi bowTie 2 3 4) = (1, -1, -1, 1) -- identical order and values. The label 4 is the residue 0 in ZMod 4 (kernel-checked: (4 : ZMod 4) = 0 by decide; chi bowTie 1 2 4 = chi bowTie 1 2 0 by rfl), and bowTie 1 = (0,0), bowTie 2 = (2,2), bowTie 3 = (0,2), bowTie 0 = (2,0) (BowTie.lean:16-22) matches K_0 = ((0,0),(2,2),(0,2),(2,0)) (def:star, sm-5-transport.tex:12-13). chi P i j k = sign det(P j - P i, P k - P i) (Chirotope.lean:10-11) is def:chirotope's chi_ijk = sgn det(mu_j - mu_i, mu_k - mu_i) (sm-1-polygons.tex:66). Turn tuple (turn bowTie 1, 2, 3, 4) = (-1, 1, 1, -1) matches (tau_1..tau_4) = (-1,+1,+1,-1) with turn P i = chi P (i-1) i (i+1) = tau_i (Chirotope.lean:13-14 vs sm-1-polygons.tex:68).

Remaining clauses also match: gcd(r, 2r+1) = 1 (line 23); shift 1 (star r) = rotationMap (starAngle r) ∘ star r with shift k P i = P (i+k) so shift 1 = sigma ((sigma P)_i = mu_{i+1}, sm-1-polygons.tex:30), rotationMap theta v = (cos theta v1 - sin theta v2, sin theta v1 + cos theta v2) the CCW rotation by theta (StarPolygons.lean:44-45), starAngle r = 2 pi r/(2r+1) (line 38); star r i = unitPoint (2r+1) (r*(i-1)) with unitPoint N k = (cos(2 pi k.val/N), sin(...)) = mu_t = u_{r(t-1)} (StarPolygons.lean:27-32 vs def:star); principalTurn P i = principalAngle (edge P (i-1)) (edge P i) = arg(conj(l_{i-1}) l_i) which is def:regular's angle in (-pi,pi) with the cos/sign spec (RegularLocus.lean:15-16, RegularPairs.lean:54, PrincipalAngles.lean:9-16); rotationNumber P = (sum principalTurn)/(2 pi) = rot (RotationNumber.lean:10-11 vs lem:rot); starNeg r = reversal (star r) with reversal P i = P (2 - i) = def:shift's (overline P)_i = mu_{2-i} (StarPolygons.lean:35, Reversal.lean:11, sm-1-polygons.tex:399-400); Generic = G1 ∧ G2 exactly def:generic (Generic.lean:11-19 vs sm-1-polygons.tex:100-106); crossingSet P = the finset of {i,j} with remote i j and E_i ∩ E_j nonempty = X(P) (Crossings.lean:12-19 vs def:crossings), so crossingSet bowTie = {{1,3}} is X(K_0) = {{1,3}}.
